Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

medusa 0.1.0

Fast C++ NIfTI matrix I/O and matrix-native event alignment

  • Added read_nifti_ts() and write_nifti_ts() for streaming C++ conversion between 3D/4D .nii/.nii.gz images and time x voxels (T x V) numeric matrices ("medusa_nifti_ts" bundles carrying voxel_map, parcel_ids, tr, and validated sform/qform geometry without allocating full 4D R arrays). Updated voxelwise_deconvolution() and backproject_medusa() to use the streaming C++ NIfTI path.
  • Added align_medusa_ts() (src/epoch_align.cpp) for C++ matrix-native event-locked alignment and multi-kernel readout quadrature ("linear", "boxcar", "triangle", "gaussian") across T x V matrices, "medusa_nifti_ts" bundles, deconvolve_crossrun_hrf() outputs, multi-run lists, and multivariate signal lists while preserving all overlap_policy, censoring, max_gap, epoch_status, align_*, time_audit, and source_clock invariants (~80x–130x faster and ~10x–135x lower peak R heap memory than legacy long-table workflows).
  • Accelerated get_medusa_interpolated_ts() and get_medusa_compression_score() on shared-clock fmri_ts objects via a zero-copy C++ matrix view (with automatic fallback for ragged per-unit clocks), added fmri_ts$to_matrix(), and upgraded evt_align_decon_files() with fast_pivot_decon_cpp(), .rds matrix-bundle support, and fork parallelism on Unix CLI/HPC.
  • Modernized file and tabular serialization across the pipeline: voxelwise_deconvolution() now supports output_format = c("csv.gz", "rds", "nifti", "parquet") (eliminating intermediate mat2df() + dplyr::left_join() expansions and writing delimited outputs via multi-threaded data.table::fwrite()); run_decon_alignment() and evt_align_decon_files() discover and align all four deconvolution formats, skip unused coordinate/status columns when reading long tables, and write aligned panels to .csv.gz, .parquet, or .rds; and mixed_by() now reads .parquet files and Hive-partitioned Parquet directories (via optional arrow) as well as .rds and delimited external_df tables, with automatic column projection and optional split_filter pushdown.
  • Unified in-memory NIfTI, cross-run HRF, deconvolution, and epoch-regression ergonomics: estimate_crossrun_hrf() and deconvolve_crossrun_hrf() now accept "medusa_nifti_ts" objects directly (auto-populating tr, spatial_groups = ts$parcel_ids, kernel_grid = hrf_library(tr, preset = "medusa"), and spatial_coords when spatial_fwhm is requested), split combined single-participant multi-run events data.frames automatically across BIDS/MEDuSA run labels, and propagate voxel_map and geometry onto "crossrun_hrf" and "crossrun_decon" so write_nifti_ts(decon, ...) and backproject_medusa(..., brain_mask = decon) need no extra reference file; decon_epoch_regression() now accepts column-name covariates (e.g., c("rpe", "abs_rpe")), one-sided formulas (~ rpe + abs_rpe), column-name trial_durations ("rt"), and combined multi-run events tables.

Standalone package extraction

  • Extracted all MEDuSA deconvolution, cross-run HRF estimation, event-locked interpolation, operator-based epoch regression, connectivity repair, NIfTI backprojection (backproject_medusa() migrated to RNifti), and split-wise multilevel modeling (mixed_by(), jlmer(), meta_mixed_by()) tools from fmri.pipeline into the standalone medusa package.

MEDuSA learning sequence, precision-weighted epoch regression, and workflow documentation

  • Add conceptual (vignettes/medusa-concepts.Rmd) and executable workflow (vignettes/medusa-workflows.Rmd) vignettes covering cross-run HRF learning, noise scaling, operator-based epoch de-mixing, duration models, per-trial precision weights, within-run ZCA whitening, NIfTI inputs, and the handoff to multilevel analysis (mixed_by(..., weights = "precision_weight")).
  • Revise the technical companion (medusa_deconvolution_review_prs_42_53.qmd) through PR #55+, align descriptions with the current implementation, distinguish legacy benchmark tables from live experiments, and add thorough inline documentation across all MEDuSA R functions.
  • decon_epoch_regression() now propagates exact run-specific AR(1) observation noise covariance through the readout and unmixing operators to compute per-trial standard errors (se_raw, se_demixed), lag-1 trial error autocorrelation (error_ac1), Empirical-Bayes stabilized precision weights (precision_weight), ZCA-whitened GLS slopes (beta_gls, se_gls), within-trial multi-lag de-mixing (demix_within_trial = TRUE), and optional within-run ZCA-whitened panel columns (whiten_panel = TRUE).
  • mixed_by() now accepts weights = "precision_weight" (normalizing positive precision weights within each split and forwarding to lme4, rstanarm, and jlmer).
  • hrf_library() adds preset = c("custom", "standard", "extended", "dense"); estimate_crossrun_hrf() adds Galwey spectral effective candidate multiplicity (hrf_effective_candidates()) and Cauchy combination parcel pooling (hrf_cauchy_p()); and deconvolve_crossrun_hrf() supports automatic prewhitened GCV tuning when lambda = NULL.

Banded linear deconvolution solver and exact Takahashi trace

  • deconvolve_reglin_cpp() now exploits the strict banded structure of Hk⊤Hk+λP+δIH_k^\top H_k + \lambda P + \delta I (half-bandwidth b=max⁡(kernel_len−1+𝕀(prewhiten),bP)b = \max(\text{kernel\_len} - 1 + \mathbb{I}(\text{prewhiten}), \; b_P)), replacing dense O(nlatent3)O(n_{\text{latent}}^3) normal-equation solves and dense matrix-RHS trace evaluations with an in-place O(nlatentb2)O(n_{\text{latent}} b^2) lower-banded Cholesky factorization, contiguous multi-signal forward/backward substitution, and the exact O(nlatentb2)O(n_{\text{latent}} b^2) Takahashi banded-inverse recursion for effective degrees of freedom tr⁡(A(λ)−1Hk⊤Hk)\operatorname{tr}(A(\lambda)^{-1} H_k^\top H_k).
  • hrf_inverse_operator_cpp(), hrf_score_run_cpp(), and hrf_noise_profile_cpp() now eliminate dense m×mm \times m AR(1) whitening matrix construction and dense O(m2L)O(m^2 L) / O(Lmm0)O(L m m_0) matrix multiplications in favor of in-place column-wise bidiagonal whitening, tridiagonal W⊤WW^\top W stencil accumulation, L1-tiled banded Cholesky solves (for nuisance_mode = "ignore"), and single-pass batch normalization across the REML noise grid.

Coefficient recovery validation

  • Test fixed window-sum and calibrated-template amplitude readouts, and regression through the frozen inverse’s transformed event design. Include active/confounded nulls, off-library HRFs, matched references and a direct forward GLS benchmark. See COEFFICIENT_RECOVERY_VALIDATION.md. These are validation candidates; package algorithms and defaults are unchanged.

Parametric recovery validation

  • Add a separate simulation study with genuine neural trial variability, task-active RPE nulls, correlated task confounds, and paired true-HRF, true-covariance, noiseless and matched-grid references. Audit coefficient bias, coverage, false positives and power across runs and independent datasets at eight fixed lambdas. Native inverse operators and trial regression factorizations are reused. See PARAMETRIC_RECOVERY_VALIDATION.md.

Noise-aware HRF evidence and event recovery diagnostics

  • Cross-run HRF fitting now defaults to pooled grid-REML AR(1) covariance, conditional GLS task/shape evidence with library corrections, training-run compatibility, and a fixed penalty toward the prespecified shape. Unsupported adaptation has an explicit parcel/prespecified fallback. Tests are conditional on the noise/mean model and are not whole-brain significance or posterior confidence. noise_model = "ols", evidence = "legacy" retains the prior fit.
  • The native inverse shares operators across HRF/noise strata and uses original acquisition times across censor gaps. AR/calibrated fits use observation masks during scaling and fitting by default. Nuisance adjustment remains explicit; optional joint projection applies to both convolution and observations. Unidentifiable covariance is reported rather than silently assumed white.
  • diagnose_crossrun_recovery() reports conditional event amplitude gain and excess leakage relative to the ideal readout, accounting for natural neural window overlap, fractional onsets, masks, and the frozen inverse. It does not automatically rescale amplitudes. See NOISE_AWARE_HRF_RECOVERY.md for review, independent reference checks, repeated validation, and throughput benchmarks.

Cross-run HRF estimation and spatial regularization

  • hrf_library() constructs a small unit-sum HRF library. estimate_crossrun_hrf() selects HRFs using other runs only, with batched Rcpp/BLAS training fits, nuisance regressors, observation masks, explicit support gates, and a recorded parcel/prespecified fallback hierarchy. Training can use condition means or free event amplitudes for signed trial responses that would otherwise average away, without supplying RPE values.
  • Explicit parcel pooling and optional voxel shape penalties toward training-derived parcel HRFs provide spatial regularization. These constrain HRF selection without spatially smoothing recovered neural activity. Strength and effect-size thresholds are user-controlled. The original heuristic mode does not supply significance tests.
  • deconvolve_crossrun_hrf() applies frozen HRFs with required fixed lambda, grouped inverse operators, bounded caching, block multiplication, and recorded per-voxel scaling. Existing NIfTI/file deconvolution defaults are unchanged. See CROSSRUN_HRF_GUIDE.md and the reproducible review/benchmark scripts.
  • HRF_ESTIMATION_VALIDATION.md reports 480 independent simulated datasets comparing learned, canonical, and true HRFs at three fixed inverse penalties. Learning helps with stable shape mismatch but can hurt with low SNR, zero-mean signed responses, run changes, or neural-duration mismatch. The original support gate accepted all null free-event fits under colored noise; support labels are not confidence measures. Estimator settings were not tuned to these results. Reproducible scripts, compact tables, and figures are included.

Auditable event overlap and impulse recovery

  • Alignment now interpolates within each unit’s valid acquisition segments before aggregation. Explicit invalid values/masks block interpolation, and brackets wider than the acquisition TR are missing by default. Off-grid median/SD now summarize interpolated units; means with changing contributors also change.
  • overlap_policy supports allow, legacy truncate, and whole-window exclude. NULL retains collision-column truncation when explicitly configured, otherwise allows overlap. valid_col, neighbor_events, and max_gap pass through file and batch alignment settings. No policy claims physiological isolation.
  • Outputs report per-lag contributor/reason counts, acquisition-time IDs and epoch reuse, neighboring events, simultaneous events, window overlap, and run edges. Source clocks are returned as attributes; file alignment adds alignment_file and writes a .sources.csv clock sidecar beside requested outputs.
